Technical Procedure
Introduction

This document 
lists the major maintenance procedure P2 of emergency diesel engine, which must 
be performed every 25000 operation hours as indicated by H 25000 in the title 
block.

The technical specifications for the diesel stated at the end of the 
document.

The first draft initiated by 
eng.: Hesham M. Hassan, reviewed by 
Maintenance director: eng. Saad Mostafa, revised by eng. Samir Abdel-Gelil at EDEPCo., accepted by maintenance general director: 
eng. Aly Mostafa Al-lithy and approved by eng. Mostafa Alam Head Sector of Talkha steam power station 2 x 
210 MW.
Safety Precautions

Work permit must be issued, the qualified maintenance staff must carry the suitable ID safety 
category.
Safety fence with caution marks surrounding the work area.

items:
Clean carefully the dismantled point 
 and the surfaces close to it with fuel oil, at complete dismantling of the 
 engine, the whole engine is cleaned.

Care is to be taken to preserve 
 cleanliness when dismantling the engine.

Wash every part in fuel oil and wipe 
 it with clean rags or with blast of compressed air

Use only suitable tools for 
 disassembly.

Take good notes of its position on 
 the engine so that reassembly may be facilitated, before dismantling any part 
 from the engine.

Be sure take note of any marks or 
 items no. on them , acc. to which they should be re-assembled. Before 
 disassembling the parts and assemblies,

Protect the engine from dirt, to 
 close the open points, cover the outlets with oiled paper and wrap the pipe 
 ends with paper.

Check whether the parts are in good 
 condition or whether they are to be repaired or replaced with new ones.

Unscrew the nuts of all bolts a turn 
 or more and then only remove all the nuts. When dismantling parts or 
 assemblies,

Be sure screw in all the bolts and 
 nuts in their original position after the parts or assemblies so that they may 
 not be lost or exchanged .Tie the shims and washers together and mark them so 
 that they may not be lost or exchanged during the re-assembly.

Take care no excessive force should 
 be applied to dismantle any part. If a big force is required, it is necessary 
 to ascertain the cause and to remove it.

Check whether the parts are suitable 
 for further use, by examining and measuring the parts, determining the 
 clearance (or interference) between contact surfaces, testing for tightness, 
 etc 
 - Replace damage or worn parts by new ones.
 - Make sure that the correct clearance or interference is 
 observed when replaced the parts 
 - Record the values of clearances, which measure during, 
 disassemble for all parts of engine in table (3).

Clean every part and lubricated the 
 moving parts with clean oil before starting to reassemble.

sections.text: Complete Engine Disassembly

items:
Drain 
 the water, lubricated oil and fuel oil from the engine and all pipes.
Close the air inlet.

Disconnect the engine from the 
 driven machine.

Dismantle the glass thermometer, the 
 instrument board and other measuring instruments and the transmitters of 
 electric instruments from the engine.

Loosen and remove all water, oil, 
 air and fuel pipes, which would hinder the dismantling of the engine.

Remove the suction tube and exhaust 
 piping from the engine cylinder heads, also the charging elbow at the 
 supercharged engine.

Dismantle the double the double fuel 
 cleaner.

Remove the starting equipment with 
 feed pipe.
Dismantle the front cover.

Dismantle the flywheel from the 
 crankshaft.

Dismantle the lateral lids and 
 covers on the engine.
Dismantle the cylinder heads.

Dismantle the valve push rods and 
 the valve push rod covers.

Dismantle the turbo-supercharger 
 with the bracket (at supercharged engine).

Dismantle the connecting rods with 
 the pistons.
Dismantle the governor
Dismantle the rear cover.
Dismantle the upper engine case.

Dismantle the lids with shells of 
 all the main bearings of the crankshaft
Dismantle the crankshaft

sections.text: Disassembly of Cylinder Head

items:
Remove the exhaust gas thermometer, 
 the cooling water thermometer and the indicator cock.
Remove the cylinder head cover.

Remove the valve push rods by 
 raising the valve rocker arms.

Remove the bolts joining the sucking 
 tube with the cylinder head.

Loosen and remove the bolts of the 
 exhaust pipe flanges at the cylinder head.

Dismantle all pipes which would 
 hinder the disassembly of the corresponding cylinder head (water collecting 
 pipe, air inlet pipe, fuel inlet / outlet pipes and oil inlet pipe And / or 
 instrument board).

Loosen gradually the nuts of the 
 cylinder head bolts for one turn and then remove them.

Screw 
 in two suspension bolts, suspend the cylinder head, moves it above the studs 
 and place it aside.

sections.text: Disassembly of the Connecting Rod with Piston

items:
Dismantle the corresponding cylinder 
 head.

Dismantle the corresponding lateral 
 cover of the upper part of the crankcase.

Remove the split pins of connecting 
 rod bolts.

Loosen and screw off the connecting 
 rod bolt-nuts. At the same time hold the lower big end lid to prevent it from 
 falling into the crankcase.
Moving out the connecting rod bolts.

Remove the Lower big end lid with 
 the shell through the hole in the lower lid of case.

Screw the suspension of piston 
 firmly on the piston crown. Clean the threads of bolts before.

Remove the pistons with the 
 connecting rod shank and shell and place it aside by means of lifting device. 
 When removing the piston, watches through the hole in the lower lid of casing 
 that the connecting rod flange does not catch the side of cylinder bush and 
 does not damage it.

Dismantle the piston after the 
 circlips have been removed and gudgeon pin has been driven out by means of 
 special fixture.

Dismantle all the pistons from 
 engine one after another from the 1st to the 6th 
 cylinder.

Turn the crankshaft on removal of 
 the flywheel, by means of a wooden beam or an iron bar placed between 3 to 4 
 bolts inserted into the holes in the crankshaft flange.

sections.text: CAUTATION:

After the 
crankshaft has been turned into the TDCs for dismantling the 2nd, 3rd, 
5th and 6th cylinders, it is necessary to secure in this 
position against swinging which might cause injury to the operator or damage to 
the engine. This may be done by securing the crankshaft in the crankcase by 
wooden beams or by two iron bars inserted between the flywheel bolts and 
bearings upon the floor.
Disassembly of Crankshaft

Separate the upper and lower engine 
case.

Remove the lids with shells of all 
crankshaft bearings.
Dismantle the counterweights.

sections.text: Assembly of Engine Parts

items:
Lubricate the friction surfaces of 
 the parts.

Protect the engine so that no dust 
 and impurities may penetrate in.

Maintain the working site clean and 
 in good order.

Take good notes of the marks and 
 items Nos. on the parts or assemblies in order to fit them in the same 
 position as before their disassembly.

Tighten the bolts and nuts crosswise 
 and gradually .Do not tighten them firmly one after another to avoid any 
 deformation of the parts.

Do not mount any other parts, unless 
 the previous part is fitted or attached correctly.

Check whether the assemblies are 
 assembled correctly and whether they can be freely turned or moved.

Use only new split pins and look- 
 washers, undamaged and new gaskets and packing.

Use only the necessary tools and 
 fixtures.

Assemble every part in reverse 
 sequence of disassembly

sections.text:
Assembly of Crankshaft 
Bearings

Assembly of the main 
Bearings

Clean thoroughly the 
seating surfaces and lubricate properly the main bearing bolts threads, nuts and 
bearing shell.

Insert the lower 
half of bearing shell into the clean bore in the lower part of the crankcase.

Insert the 
Crankshaft. Fit the upper half of bearing shell with the cap ( Observe the 
numbering of the caps and shells)

Tighten firmly the 
nuts (So that the shell seats down), loosen them and tighten again.

Tighten alternately 
and uniformly the nuts to the line of marking of nut and shell marked by marker.

Check the 
clearances. In vertical plan the clearance must be within 0.17 - 0.256 mm in the 
plan measured 10 mm from the dividing plan of both sides and on both bridges it 
must be for 0.02 - 0.1 mm larger than the clearance measured in the vertical plan.

Assemble every part 
in reverse sequence of disassembly.

Assembly of the 
Big end Bearings

Clean thoroughly the 
seating surfaces and lubricate properly the connecting rod bolts.

Measure the 
connecting rod bolt in loose condition by using the measuring yoke supplied with 
the engine tools and indicated by the engine No. and the nominal length of bolts 
which inserting feelers between the recessed end of bolt and the seating surface 
of the yoke .Fig(3)

Fit the connecting 
rod lid with shell and inserted connecting rod bolts to the crankshaft pin and 
connecting rod shackle and connecting rod bolts are lightly tightened by nuts

(Observe the numbering on 
the connecting rod and bolts)

Tighten the nuts 
(acc. to the tightening of main bolt joints).

Assemble every part 
in reverse sequence of disassembly.

sections.text:
Assembly of Cylinder 
Heads

Be sure the gaskets 
used must be straight, not damaged and annealed.

Place the gasket on 
the cylinder liner and centered accurately so that it may not protrude over the 
edge of the liner and fits properly in the recess.

Mount the cylinder 
head on the bolts and fit it to the cylinder liner so that the gasket is not 
shifted or reformatted.

Check the seating of 
the cylinder head and gasket whether the gasket is not squeezed at any point. 
Replace the gasket if damaged.

Set the valve 
clearance see clearance table (Table No. 1).

The nuts of cylinder 
head bolts should be tighten (acc. to the tightening of main bolt joints).

Assemble every part 
in reverse sequence of disassembly.

sections.text:
Tightening of main 
Bolt Joints

Tightening of cylinder 
Head Bolt Nuts

Be sure the nuts of 
cylinder head tightened crosswise by means of the cylinder head spanner extended 
with a bar.

Do the tightening in 
two steps.
- First, all cylinder head 
nuts are tightened for the bolt prolongation of approx. 0.15-mm.
- The next, tightening is done for the prolongation of bolt of 0.25-0.3 mm. 
After the engine has been started a check for tightness is made

Bolts prolongation 
is measured by depth gauge with vernier accuracy of 0.02 mm.

During measurement, 
arms of gauge are supported on the upper surface of nut and the movable part is 
moved out so that it touches the ground bolt surface in nut.

The difference 
between measured values before and after the tightening of the cylinder head 
bolts means the value of bolt prolongation.

sections.text:
Tightening of 
connecting Rod Bolt Nuts

Check the connecting 
rod surface from the mechanical break of surface or any defect. If the 
mechanical break is larger, bolts must be exchanged.

Replace all bolts 
with found permanent deformation larger than 0.1 mm (permanent bolt prolongation 
at free state).

Measure the length 
of bolt at free state by means of measuring shackle by underputting the feeler 
gauge between the recessed bolt end and shackle seating (See Fig 4). The 
clearance A can be found from the clearance table (Table 1).

Assemble the 
connecting rod bolts acc. to prescript numbering as shown in Fig (3).

Be sure the nuts of 
the connecting rod Bolts are crosswise tightened to the line of marking of nut 
and bolt which corresponds to prescript prolongation of connecting rod bolts 
(0.2 0.28 mm) up to position of a cut in a nut and a hole in a bolt for a 
split pin.

Measure the 
connecting rod bolts prolongation by measuring shackle and feeler as shown in 
Fig (4).

After tightening the nuts of the 
connecting rod bolts they are ensured by a split pin which must be not move 
after its opening.

sections.text:
Tightening of 
Bolt Nuts of Main Bearings

Be 
sure the upper shell and the bearing lids are assembled.

Tighten all nuts crosswise to the line 
of nuts and shell marking for the given prolongation (0.22 to 0.26 mm) marked by 
manufacturer.
Check the clearance.

Lock the nuts against loosening by a 
lock.

Be sure prolongation check is not 
carried out, unless at bolt exchange by means of dial indicator as shown in Fig 
(5).

Mark identically the nuts and bolts 
again by a line.

Be sure under this tightening the 
bolts must have an extension of 0.22-0.26 mm.

Cleaning of lubricating oil

Clean the oil either by 
means of two type RHO 3a centrifugal cleaners at the discharge of oil pump of a 
capacity of 600 l/hr, at a pressure 0.2 Mpa which operate continuously or by an 
independent electric centrifuge included in the engine room equipment, which is 
started at certain interval acc. to its out put , so that the cleaned quantity 
corresponds to the quantity cleaned by two RHO 3a units with this alternative 
the RHO 3a centrifugal cleaners are not necessary.
